acceptance.command:
grep -cF 'send `SIGHUP` to log it again' docs/operation.md
grep -cxF 'An invalid or unreadable file is not applied. The API keeps the running configuration and logs one `warn` line, `config reload rejected: <path>: <message>` (the message never quotes a value), and counts `pulse_api_config_reload_total{result="invalid"}`. A rejection is logged and counted only when its line differs from the last reload warning. Looks and `SIGHUP` share that memory: a `SIGHUP`, or a look that sees a changed file, reads the bad file again, but while the line stays the same it logs nothing and counts nothing, also when the bytes changed. A rejection with another message is logged and counted. After a valid file is applied, the same bad file is logged and counted again. An unreadable file is read again at every look, so fixing its permissions applies it without a `SIGHUP`. Database check writes still work while the file is broken.' docs/operation.md

Read every added line yourself and list every added comment in the PR body, including inline comments and the rewritten parseConfigText doc comment. Say none only after this complete read finds none. No new test file is in scope; any later approved revision adding one permits at most one explanatory comment line naming the class and expected outcome.

Performance impact evidence: run five interleaved BASE/candidate pairs of this full-suite command on the same shared machine with Bun 1.4.0, matched installs and tracked coverage config; never concurrently. Record user plus system CPU including children, exit status and pass count for all ten runs. Median per side is the third sorted value; report candidate minus BASE to 0.01 s and percent of BASE median to 0.1%. Informational only, no Docker bench or unsupported runtime regression gate.
